node-1.label: Right scrotal swelling rapidly growing over 3 months without local pain

node-2.label: Patient is a 50-year-old Japanese man, non-smoker, with medical history of hypertension treated with ARB tablet daily and no known allergies

node-3.label: Swelling developed over 3 months with no history of trauma or infections including STDs

node-4.label: Puncture at a prior hospital yielded red-colored fluid; physical examination confirmed right scrotal swelling

why.why: Pathologist's histopathology refutes malignancy: bland tall columnar cells, WT-1+/ER+/PR+, calretinin−/D2-40−, no invasion or papillary growth. Radiologist's imaging shows a multilocular cystic lesion without solid components or contrast enhancement. These findings directly contradict a malignant scrotal tumor, so confidence is reduced from 0.7 to 0.03.

Imaging confirms a multilocular fluid-filled cystic lesion with hemorrhagic signal, which could suggest a benign fluid collection; however histopathology identifies a benign multicystic mesothelial lesion rather than a simple hematocele, so confidence decreases from 0.15 to 0.12.

No pain, no infection/STD history, red non-purulent fluid, and histopathology/imaging showing a benign cystic mesothelial lesion without inflammatory features further refute infectious/inflammatory causes; confidence is reduced to 0.02.
Trauma was explicitly denied, and imaging/histopathology demonstrate a multilocular cystic mesothelial lesion rather than traumatic injury; confidence is reduced to 0.02.

node-9.label: Histopathology shows bland tall columnar mesothelial cells with WT-1+/ER+/PR+, calretinin−/D2-40−, no invasion or papillary growth

node-10.label: Ultrasound and MRI reveal a multilocular cystic lesion with septa attached to the testis, lacking solid components or contrast enhancement

node-11.label: MRI signal of the scrotal lesion is consistent with hematoma/hemorrhagic fluid

node-12.label: Scrotal benign multicystic mesothelial lesion (multilocular peritoneal inclusion cyst/cystadenoma)
